Thought: I need to analyze the mass spectrum of phenol to determine the relative intensity of the m/z 95 peak compared to the molecular ion peak at m/z 94.

In mass spectrometry, the molecular ion peak (M+) represents the intact molecule after losing one electron. For phenol (C6H5OH), this would appear at m/z 94.

The m/z 95 peak would represent the M+1 peak, which is typically due to the natural abundance of heavier isotopes (like 13C instead of 12C) in some molecules.

The question asks about the relative intensity of the m/z 95 peak compared to the molecular ion peak. This is typically expressed as a percentage.

Looking at the options, I need to determine which percentage correctly represents this intensity ratio. This requires knowledge of phenol's mass spectrum data.

Based on standard mass spectral data for phenol, the M+1 peak (m/z 95) typically has an intensity of about 6-7% relative to the molecular ion peak (m/z 94).
Final Answer: The question asks about the relative intensity of the m/z 95 peak compared to the molecular ion peak (m/z 94) in phenol's mass spectrum. The m/z 95 peak represents the M+1 peak, which is due to the natural abundance of heavier isotopes. Based on standard mass spectral data for phenol, the relative intensity of the m/z 95 peak is approximately 6.6% of the molecular ion peak.
